purpose: A non-modal floating panel anchored to a trigger for rich, interactive content: optional media, a title, a description, a content slot and footer actions. It opens on click, never on hover.

notFor.case: A short hint shown on hover or focus that holds no actions.
A list of commands behind a button.
Picking a date from a field.
A blocking decision or a task that needs full attention.

Open.meaning: Opened from its trigger (by the person, or by the app through open).
Open.visual: Panel on Surface/layer-2 with a Border/default stroke (Stroke/divider) and the popover-md lift (popover-lg at lg); the arrow in Surface/layer-2 edged with Border/default; title Content/primary, description and content Content/secondary. Enters on popover-enter.

Closed.visual: Not rendered. Leaves on popover-exit and focus returns to the trigger.

a11y.keyboard: Space or Enter on the trigger opens and closes it; Tab moves through the content; Escape or an outside click closes it and returns focus to the trigger.
a11y.reducedMotion: Fades in and out instead of popping (the popover-enter / popover-exit reduced-motion bodies in lib/motion.ts).
notes: The trigger gets aria-haspopup and aria-expanded; label the panel with aria-labelledby on the title.
Keep one primary action inside at most.

openQuestions: On mobile, should a Popover become a bottom Sheet (as the AuthSignInPhone screens draw it) or stay anchored on every viewport? (finding DOC-002 AuthSignInPhone)
Figma keeps the panel stroke at a literal 1 with no variable while the arrow binds Stroke/divider (popover-contract.md). Should the panel bind Stroke/divider in Figma as code does?
